correctness.rationale: Reconstructed for all n≥4 and real α>1: first synchronous update maps each initial-2 to 1 and kills each initial-1, so N_i(1)=X_i. The next sign is sign(1−α(X_{i−1}+X_{i+1})/2), producing exactly isolated survivors, two-run dimers or long-run endpoints, with equality α=2 checked separately. Distinct initial runs are insulated by absorbing zeroes; dimer (2,2)↔(1,1) below α=2 and (1,1) fixed at equality. Local fair iid three-bit probabilities give 3/8 and 1/8 for every finite n≥4; four-bit 0110 gives 1/8 dimer sites, hence fixed sites 1/4 and biomass means. Only all-zero/all-one X cause global extinction for α≤2, probability 2^{1−n}; disjoint four-block events yield the period-two lower bound. New independent exhaustive state transitions confirm 10,160 (n, α, initial-state) cases but do not prove the all-n claim.
residual_risks: Quantification is only n≥4, α>1, deterministic synchronous update and initially positive {1,2} biomasses.
Finite exhaustive n≤10 corroboration is not substituted for the run-induction argument.

Assigned RESULT.md: full classification and exact finite-size probability law
value.rationale: The degree-two cycle is the canonical exactly solvable spatial ecology baseline for the originating random-network competition map. A complete basin classification, two distinct sharp competition transitions and all-finite-n 3/8-to-1/8 occupied fraction identify the mechanism behind fixed patches versus synchronized dimers. The exact extinction probability and exponentially high probability of two-cycle occurrence under fair initial states are natural measurements, not arbitrary numerical curiosities.
residual_risks: Relevance is mathematical benchmarking and dynamic mechanism, not claims about real ecosystems, higher-dimensional interaction graphs or measured empirical phase diagrams.

limitations: Only n≥4, α>1, K=2, synchronous cycle update and initial {1,2} biomass. No claims for other graphs or nonuniform draws.
